facts.statement: Neuquensaurus lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 74.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Neuquensaurus (meaning "Neuquén lizard") is a genus of saltasaurid sauropod dinosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous, about 83-74.5 million years ago in Argentina in South America.

facts.statement: The genus Neuquensaurus likely included one or two species of titanosaurian sauropods living in South America during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, about 80 million years ago.
facts.quote: Neuquensaurus ("lagarto de Neuquén") es un género representado por una, posiblemente dos, especies de dinosaurios saurópodos titanosaurianos, que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 80 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Fossils of Neuquensaurus were found in the Anacleto Formation near the Neuquén River in Argentina.
facts.quote: Its fossils were recovered from outcrops of the Anacleto Formation around Cinco Saltos, near the Neuquén river from which its name is derived.

facts.statement: Richard Lydekker originally named the species Titanosaurus australis in 1893 based on tail vertebrae and limb bones.
facts.quote: In 1893, Richard Lydekker named Titanosaurus australis, based on a series of caudal vertebrae and limb elements.

facts.statement: Jaime Eduardo Powell validly established the genus Neuquensaurus in 1992, transferring the type species to Neuquensaurus australis.
facts.quote: In 1992 Powell validly named Neuquensaurus, with as type species Titanosaurus australis of which the combinatio nova then is Neuquensaurus australis.

facts.statement: Neuquensaurus is classified as a derived saltasaurine, closely related to Saltasaurus, Rocasaurus, and Bonatitan.
facts.quote: Neuquensaurus is a derived saltasaurine. Its closest relatives were Saltasaurus, Rocasaurus, and Bonatitan, and together they made up Saltasaurinae.

facts.statement: Neuquensaurus is believed to have had armor-like osteoderms on its body.
facts.quote: This dinosaur is believed to have possessed armor-like osteoderms.

facts.statement: Neuquensaurus was a relatively small sauropod with a femur measuring 0.75 meters, reaching lengths of 7 to 9 meters and weighing between 1.8 and 3.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: A relatively small sauropod, with a femur only 0.75 m long. It is one of the most completely known of Patagonian sauropods, measuring 7 - 9 m long and weighing 1.8 - 3.5 MT.

facts.statement: Neuquensaurus is unique among sauropods for having a sacrum composed of seven vertebrae.
facts.quote: Unique among all sauropods, the sacrum of Neuquensaurus is composed of seven vertebrae.

facts.statement: The scapula of Neuquensaurus resembles those of Saltasaurus, Opisthocoelicaudia, Lirainosaurus, and Alamosaurus.
facts.quote: In general aspect, the scapula resembles Saltasaurus, Opisthocoelicaudia, Lirainosaurus, and Alamosaurus.

facts.statement: In Neuquensaurus, the scapula is fused with the coracoid, a trait also seen in Opisthocoelicaudia.
facts.quote: The scapula is co-ossified with the coracoid, a feature also found in Opisthocoelicaudia.

facts.statement: Analysis of vertebral centra suggests two distinct morphotypes in Neuquensaurus, potentially supporting the hypothesis that two different species existed.
facts.quote: Geometric morphometric analysis of the vertebral centra of Neuquensaurus suggests that two distinct morphotypes existed, one of which had four spinoprezygapophyseal laminae and included specimens assigned to both N. australis and N. robustus, potentially lending validity to the hypothesis that two different species of Neuquensaurus existed.

facts.statement: John Stanton McIntosh assigned the species to the genus Saltasaurus in 1990, arguing the differences were not taxonomically significant enough for a separate genus.
facts.quote: In 1990, the two species were assigned to Saltasaurus by John Stanton McIntosh, as a Saltasaurus australis and a Saltasaurus robustus, claiming that the features found by Bonaparte were not of sufficient taxonomic importance to justify a generic separation.

facts.statement: Powell considered the species N. robustus to be non-diagnostic and classified it as a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: He also found Titanosaurus robustus to be assignable to the new genus, but considered it non-diagnostical, and so a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Neuquensaurus grew to be 8 meters long and 3 meters tall.
facts.quote: Neuquensaurus llegó a medir 8 metros de largo y 3 metros de alto.

facts.statement: Researchers believe this dinosaur possessed osteoderms shaped like armor.
facts.quote: Se cree que este dinosaurio poseía osteodermos con forma de armadura.

facts.statement: It was a relatively small sauropod with a femur measuring only 0.75 meters in length.
facts.quote: Un saurópodo relativamente pequeño, con un fémur de solo 0,75 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The sacrum of Neuquensaurus is composed of seven vertebrae, a unique trait among sauropods.
facts.quote: El sacro de Neuquensaurus se compone de siete vértebras.

facts.statement: A 2008 study reconstructed the hind limb muscles of Neuquensaurus.
facts.quote: En 2008 se realizó una reconstrucción muscular del miembro trasero de un Neuquensaurus.

facts.statement: Powell validly named Neuquensaurus in 1992, designating Neuquensaurus australis as the valid combination.
facts.quote: En 1992 Powell nombró válidamente Neuquensaurus, con la especie tipo Titanosaurus australis, de la cual la combinatio nova es Neuquensaurus australis.

facts.statement: Neuquensaurus is a derived saltasaurine within the subfamily Saltasaurinae.
facts.quote: Neuquensaurus es una saltasáurido derivado dentro de la subfamilia Saltasaurinae.

facts.statement: Its closest relatives were Saltasaurus, Rocasaurus, and Bonatitan.
facts.quote: Sus parientes más cercanos eran Saltasaurus, Rocasaurus y Bonatitan.

facts.statement: Neuquensaurus lived from the Santonian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 85.7 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Maastrichtian (85.7 to 66 million years ago)
